step1: A constant-nonzero-Jacobian birational target map and its inverse are defined on the respective old affine planes as maps to P2; resolution centres may therefore be confined to old infinity.
step2: The strict transform of a branch component retains its old-affine singular point. A prime exceptional for a smooth-surface birational morphism is smooth rational, so this singular curve is not contracted. If its image were the new infinity P1, the proper birational curve map would be finite and hence an isomorphism because P1 is normal, again contradicting singularity.
step3: Birational identification preserves distinct generic curve valuations and their K/E ramification/residue data. Distinct selected base components cannot merge into one target prime.
step4: For L/K of degree m, an old ramified place remains ramified by multiplicativity. Above old unramified places, the sum of unramified residue degrees is at most m times the old residue degree. Hence new ramified e*f mass above D_i is at least m(n-u_i)=m w_i.
step5: In the finite normalization for the polynomial Keller pair, every ramified height-one prime above an affine D_i lies outside the whole source A2 because the restriction is etale. Its all-Keller contribution r_j delta_j equals its divisorial e*f mass. Distinct D_i index disjoint source-prime subsets, so there is no double counting.
step6: With N=mn, the all-Keller budget gives mn-1>=sum r_j delta_j>=m sum_i w_i>=mn, contradiction.
scope: The theorem is conditional on the named symplectic birational and all-Keller foundations and applies only when the stated old-affine singular branch components and threshold are actually established. It is not donor classification, uniform generation, N=1, JC2, or an eligibility result for the excluded optional client.
